answer: One concrete mechanism: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because ivory only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. In practice ocean is enforced by the ledger itself: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any yarrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
